_comment: The horizontal frame bar, spanning only x 2..14 - the span BETWEEN the two corner cubes.
It used to run the full 0..16, which overlapped energy_cell_edge_v in the 2x2x2 corner. Flush,
their north/down faces were exactly coplanar and the corners flickered; offset by 0.01 they were
near-coplanar, which is worse (no deterministic tie-break, so depth precision decides per-pixel
and the whole frame shimmers); offset by 0.05 the bar no longer reached the block edge and left a
visible bright seam. There is no good value - the overlap itself is the bug.
Now the corners are owned by exactly one model, always: edge_v when the perpendicular face is
exposed, and energy_cell_edge_cap when it is not (i.e. a neighbouring cell is there, so edge_v is
not emitted). Those two conditions are mutually exclusive, so nothing is ever drawn twice and no
corner is ever left empty. Everything can then sit flush and there is neither a gap nor a
